directions.label: Clean Premium Commerce
directions.approach: Calm and restrained. Lower density, generous whitespace, a quiet header, large product imagery, and merchandising content used sparingly so the product carries each view.

directions.label: Editorial Modern Retail
directions.approach: Composed like a publication. Larger editorial blocks set among the products, strong typographic hierarchy, imagery that dominates, and grids that vary rather than repeat.

directions.label: Dynamic Contemporary Ecommerce
directions.approach: Energetic and efficient. Higher density, more products in view, prominent merchandising rails and badges, a utility-forward header, and the purchase actions kept close at hand.

directions_note: The labels are descriptive only. They are three structural approaches to hierarchy, density, composition and interaction, not three brand identities. All three satisfy the same scope, draw the same states, keep every pattern the contract fixes, and stay neutral. They may differ only in presentation and in interaction choices that are genuinely open. None adds a feature.

IX-09 stands: one prominent hero, never an autoplaying carousel. Category shortcuts (HOME-05) and the featured collections (HOME-04) are separate sections, and trending (HOME-02) and new arrivals (HOME-03) are separate, independently managed sections. Purposeful motion is allowed where it never obstructs shopping or costs performance.

The checkout stands: DQ-03's one page with C's presentation, every required review item before Place Order, the condensed header with the logo, search, account, wishlist, cart and language switcher, and no express delivery in the first release (SHIP-07, P2).
DQ-01 and DQ-02 stay provisional: Western digits and native numbered pagination are the working baselines, and Load More is not newly authorised.

Motion: purposeful microinteractions, accessible overlays and meaningful feedback; no compulsory carousel motion, no scroll-jacking and no animation that delays a purchase; reduced motion and mobile performance are design constraints. A Lighthouse score of 99 to 100 is an aspirational engineering target, not a contractual guarantee.

Account, batches 04 and 06: a coherent desktop sidebar and mobile account navigation, a dashboard with recent orders and their statuses, clear profile and password sections, and accurate verification, cart-merge, recovery and account-security states. open_decision.recommendation: Claude Design recommends confirming the add in place in the buy area: the button shows Adding, then a tick; a confirmation under it names the item, variant and quantity, with View cart and Checkout; the header count steps up on success only; one polite live announcement; focus stays on Add to cart; the mini-cart drawer opens only on a deliberate press of the header cart. A failed add shows its error in the same place, with role=alert, no count change and no add_to_cart event. Drawn in sf-pdp-simple (adding, added, from the mobile bar, and a failed add) and sf-pdp-variable (selected, no_selection).
open_decision.rationale: The visitor is still deciding on the product page; an inline confirmation keeps them there, follows the rule IX-02 already locks for quick adds, keeps focus where it was, and avoids stacking a drawer over the mobile buy bar. Cart and checkout stay one press away. The alternative, the mini-cart drawer as a focused confirmation, keeps the free-shipping prompt (CART-07) in view after an add, at the cost of a modal layer, moved focus and a second behaviour for the same action.
open_decision.not_a_lock: Recorded as a recommendation for the owner's batch-03 review. It is not a lock, and interaction-options.json is unchanged.
open_decision.alignment_pending: The inventory note on sf-pdp-simple:added reads "Mini-cart shown". It predates IX-10 and does not match the drawn recommendation. It is deliberately left unchanged in this import; the inventory and its brief need aligning once IX-10 is decided, whichever pattern is chosen.
open_decision.review_point: The in-page confirmation stays until the quantity changes or the visitor adds again. The confirmation on the mobile buy bar is drawn to return to one row when the visitor scrolls on, or after about five seconds without focus inside it. A keyboard user keeps it, since focus stays on the bar's Add to cart; a touch or screen-reader user who has not moved focus loses the View cart and Checkout links after five seconds, with the header cart as the remaining route. Whether the bar's confirmation should also persist, or collapse only on scroll, is part of the IX-10 decision. It has no close control, and a non-modal confirmation needs none.

provisional_assumptions.item: AUTH-02, registration with a phone number
provisional_assumptions.status: Drawn as an optional phone field on the email and password form, with no one-time code and no SMS verification. That is a provisional design assumption, not confirmed compliance. The signed row is "Register with phone number", P1-L, and P1-L means a reduced specification listed in Part One section 1.2, but section 1.2 lists no reduction for AUTH-02, so its launch boundary is undefined. Collecting an optional number is not the same as letting a customer register with a phone number: registration by phone makes the number an account identifier, and usually means proving the customer holds it, while SMS is INT-07 (P2, not contracted) and notifications are email only at launch.
provisional_assumptions.needs_clarification: What AUTH-02's reduced specification is; whether a phone number may be the identifier a customer registers and signs in with at launch, and if so how it is proved without SMS; and whether an optional phone field on email registration satisfies the row.

native.meaning: A standard screen already does the work. The addition is a filter, a field, a count or a link, drawn in place on an annotated standard screen.

constrained.meaning: A platform mechanism (the block editor, global styles, the standard product, coupon or order screen, or the document mechanism selected in its PBI) shapes a real addition. Drawn inside that mechanism.

annotate_only.meaning: The interface belongs to the standard administration, a provider or an existing build. Only the states, the handoff or the extension are annotated. Not redrawn.

custom.meaning: No standard screen exists. A new screen or panel, drawn in the standard administration idiom, never a bespoke administration interface.
